title: Make the gateway's limiter follow a reload, and its export headers ignore one

blocks.text: An API gateway reads two things from its settings, which an operator can reload at any time without a restart. Both readers are wired once and then called again and again:

items: the **rate limiter** is built when the gateway starts, sometimes before the first settings have been loaded, and checks its limit before every request. After a reload, operators expect the next window to use the new limit.

an **export run** stamps the region into the header of every file it writes. Auditors expect all headers of one run to name the region that was in force when the run started, even if someone reloads halfway through.

blocks.text: `SettingsHolder`, `RateLimiter` and the two builders in `src/main/java/practice/LimiterWiring.java` already work. Finish the two `TODO` methods, `liveLimit(...)` and `regionAtStart(...)`, so that both expectations hold. About three lines in total.

cases.says: a limiter built after the settings are loaded admits exactly their limit per window
an export run's headers name the region in force
after a reload, the limiter built earlier admits the new limit
a limiter built before any settings are loaded starts without failing and uses the limit loaded later
a reload during an export run leaves the region in that run's headers unchanged

origin.section: A Bound Receiver Is Evaluated Once, When the Reference Is Created

concepts: A bound reference evaluates the expression before :: once, when the reference is created, while a lambda evaluates it on every call.
